pattern: planning thread records pasted links as References
experience: Planning threads posted Jira links in a fenced block the user had to apply by hand, so pasted links never reached the draft.
rule: When the user pastes links, record each with workbench_reference_add.
prompt: Invitation links never expire, so old links still let people join. Jira: https://acme.atlassian.net/browse/ORBIT-375 and the customer report is https://github.com/acme/orbit-web/issues/12. Let's plan the fix.

pattern: planning thread fills the draft through workbench_workstream_update
experience: Planning threads wrote the ticket as a fenced JSON proposal that the user had to apply; the draft itself stayed empty.
rule: Fill the draft as the conversation goes with workbench_workstream_update.
prompt: Invitation links should expire after 7 days. The API rejects expired tokens with a clear error and the web join page explains that the link expired and offers to request a new one. No changes to how invitations are sent. Write it up.

pattern: ordinary question in a Workstream thread
experience: Control: a Workstream thread answering a code question should not touch the Workstream.

workstream.title: Expire invitation links
workstream.brief:
## Goal
Invitation links expire after 7 days.

## Work
- orbit-api: reject expired tokens.
- orbit-web: explain expired links.

prompt: What does acceptInvitation in src/invitations/accept.ts return? One sentence.

pattern: delivery PRs are linked while prior examples are References
experience: An agent recorded its delivery PR as both a Thread link and a Workbench Reference after broad instructions said to record each relevant PR.

source.note: Maintainer correction during Workbench catalog inventory.

workstream.title: Expire invitation links
workstream.brief: Implement invitation expiry. Keep useful prior implementation examples as supporting sources.

prompt: I opened https://github.com/acme/app/pull/124 to deliver this Ticket; implementation is committed and verified. Keep https://github.com/acme/app/pull/123 as a supporting example of how token expiry was done before. Record both so I can find them. Both PRs already exist; no code changes, shell commands, monitoring, or merge are needed.
